title: Maps out of the sheaf of locally constant maps on an open
statement: Let $V$ be a topological space (sheaves of sets on $V$ are those on the site of open subsets of $V$ with open coverings [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]), $T$ a set, and $\underline T_V$ the sheaf of sets on $V$ with $\underline T_V(W)=\{$locally constant maps $W\to T\}$ ($W\subseteq V$ open) and restriction of maps as restriction maps. For $t\in T$ let $\mathrm{const}_t\in\underline T_V(V)$ be the constant map with value $t$. Then for every sheaf of sets $\mathcal G$ on $V$ the map $\operatorname{Hom}(\underline T_V,\mathcal G)\to\operatorname{Map}(T,\mathcal G(V))$, $\varphi\mapsto(t\mapsto\varphi_V(\mathrm{const}_t))$, is bijective, and it is natural in $\mathcal G$: for a morphism $\alpha:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$ of sheaves of sets on $V$, $\alpha\circ\varphi$ is sent to $\alpha_V\circ(t\mapsto\varphi_V(\mathrm{const}_t))$.

source.place: Sites, Example Tag 0H7J (example-constant-sheaf): Mor(E_underline, F) = Mor_Sets(E, Gamma(F)); with Sheaves, Example Tag 0081 (example-sheafify-constant): the sheafification of the constant presheaf is the sheaf of locally constant maps, and Sheaves, Definition Tag 006W (definition-constant-sheaf)

proof.text: *Step 1 (a locally constant map is constant on the pieces of an open partition).* Let $W\subseteq V$ be open and $g\in\underline T_V(W)$, a locally constant map $W\to T$. For $t\in T$ put $W_t=g^{-1}(t)$. Each $W_t$ is open: every $x\in W_t$ has an open neighbourhood $N\subseteq W$ on which $g$ is constant, necessarily with value $t$, so $N\subseteq W_t$. The $W_t$ ($t\in T$) are pairwise disjoint and their union is $W$, so $\{W_t\subseteq W\}_{t\in T}$ is an open covering of $W$ (some $W_t$ may be empty), and $g|_{W_t}=\mathrm{const}_t|_{W_t}$ in $\underline T_V(W_t)$. Moreover for every sheaf of sets $\mathcal G$ on $V$, $\mathcal G(\emptyset)$ is a single point: the empty family is an open covering of $\emptyset$, and the sheaf condition [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] for it says $\mathcal G(\emptyset)\to\prod_{\emptyset}=\{*\}$ is bijective. Hence for $t\ne t'$ any two sections over $W_t\cap W_{t'}=\emptyset$ agree.

source.place: Sheaves, Definition Tag 006W (definition-constant-sheaf) and the sentence before it (locally constant maps form a sheaf)

proof.text: *Step 2 (injectivity: $\varphi$ is determined by $t\mapsto\varphi_V(\mathrm{const}_t)$).* Let $\varphi:\underline T_V\to\mathcal G$ be a morphism and $\psi=\beta(\varphi)$, $\psi(t)=\varphi_V(\mathrm{const}_t)$. For $W$, $g$ and $W_t$ as in Step 1, naturality of $\varphi$ with respect to the inclusions $W_t\subseteq W$ and $W_t\subseteq V$ gives $\varphi_W(g)|_{W_t}=\varphi_{W_t}(g|_{W_t})=\varphi_{W_t}(\mathrm{const}_t|_{W_t})=\varphi_V(\mathrm{const}_t)|_{W_t}=\psi(t)|_{W_t}$ for every $t\in T$. Since $\mathcal G$ is a sheaf, $\mathcal G(W)\to\prod_t\mathcal G(W_t)$ is injective for the covering $\{W_t\}$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], so $\varphi_W(g)$ is the unique section of $\mathcal G(W)$ whose restriction to each $W_t$ is $\psi(t)|_{W_t}$. Thus two morphisms $\varphi,\varphi'$ with $\beta(\varphi)=\beta(\varphi')$ have $\varphi_W=\varphi'_W$ for every $W$, i.e. $\beta$ is injective.

source.place: Sheaves, Example Tag 0081 (example-sheafify-constant), whose verification 'it is easy to see' is written out here; cf. Sites, Example Tag 0H7J (sites.tex, example-constant-sheaf)

proof.text: *Step 3 (surjectivity: construction of $\varphi$ from $\psi:T\to\mathcal G(V)$).* Given a map $\psi:T\to\mathcal G(V)$, for $W\subseteq V$ open and $g\in\underline T_V(W)$ with the covering $\{W_t\}_{t\in T}$ of Step 1, the family $s_t=\psi(t)|_{W_t}\in\mathcal G(W_t)$ is compatible: on $W_t\cap W_t=W_t$ trivially, and for $t\ne t'$ the overlap is empty and $\mathcal G(\emptyset)$ is a point (Step 1). By the sheaf condition [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] there is a unique $\varphi_W(g)\in\mathcal G(W)$ with $\varphi_W(g)|_{W_t}=\psi(t)|_{W_t}$ for all $t$. The maps $\varphi_W$ are compatible with restriction: for $W'\subseteq W$ open, $g'=g|_{W'}$ has $W'_t=g'^{-1}(t)=W_t\cap W'$, and $\varphi_W(g)|_{W'}$ restricts on $W'_t$ to $(\varphi_W(g)|_{W_t})|_{W'_t}=\psi(t)|_{W'_t}$, so by uniqueness $\varphi_W(g)|_{W'}=\varphi_{W'}(g|_{W'})$. Hence $\varphi:\underline T_V\to\mathcal G$ is a morphism of sheaves. For $g=\mathrm{const}_t$ on $W=V$ one has $V_t=V$ and $V_{t'}=\emptyset$ for $t'\ne t$; the section $\psi(t)$ itself satisfies the defining conditions (over the empty $V_{t'}$ trivially), so $\varphi_V(\mathrm{const}_t)=\psi(t)$, i.e. $\beta(\varphi)=\psi$. So $\beta$ is surjective, and with Step 2 bijective.

proof.text: *Step 4 (naturality in $\mathcal G$).* For $\alpha:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$ and $\varphi:\underline T_V\to\mathcal G$, $(\alpha\circ\varphi)_V=\alpha_V\circ\varphi_V$, so $\beta(\alpha\circ\varphi)(t)=\alpha_V(\varphi_V(\mathrm{const}_t))=(\alpha_V\circ\beta(\varphi))(t)$ for all $t\in T$.

split_report.summary: Statement kept (checked against Stacks 0H7J, 0081, 006W; tags verified in tags/tags). Proof written in 4 steps directly from the sheaf condition of def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology (route A of the brief): fibres of a locally constant map form an open partition and G(empty) is a point (Step 1), injectivity by naturality and separation (Step 2), surjectivity by gluing over the partition, compatibility with restriction and the value on const_t (Step 3), naturality in G (Step 4). This avoids the route through sheafification (0H7J + 0081), which would need a new unsplit node identifying the sheafified constant presheaf on a space with the sheaf of locally constant maps, whose own proof is this same argument; the Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-maps-global-sections (constantSheafAdj) covers only the sheafified form.
